transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Who are you. Keep your voice low — this place is dangerous.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am Salim. I came down here to find my brother Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Names fade quickly in this place. Turn back now before you forget who you are searching for.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am not leaving without him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then steady yourself. The things watching from those stone houses can sense fear, and panic only feeds the dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Have you seen him pass by this fountain?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I try not to study the faces of the lost. It is safer to watch the oil than to stare too long at shadows.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: He is the only family I have left.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Then hold onto that. This place tries to make you numb, and if you stop caring, you are already fading.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Tell me how to survive long enough to find him.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Keep your voice low and your hands away from the oil. It burns more than skin — it eats at what you remember.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What else should I guard against?

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Guard your mind. The well steals from inside first. If you let his name slip, he will become a stranger to you.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will never forget Omar.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't say that so loud. The watchers wait for pride as much as fear.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: It feels like the shadows are pressing against me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: That weight does not leave. You move through it or it swallows you. There is no third choice down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I don't know if I am strong enough alone.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: I cannot leave this fountain. But I can give you something to carry. A shield for your mind.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: What kind of shield.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Words. A rhythm to keep your thoughts steady when the silence grows loud and the dark tries to get inside.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Give them to me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: My jaw aches reaching for them. Say them once and mean them — don't repeat them. The square listens for echoes.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will mean every word.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break. Say it once so I know it is yours.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Courage in my chest. Fire in my will. I do not break.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Good. There is one more — harder to give. My hands won't stop shaking. This is what speaking costs down here.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I am still listening.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Prayer for the lost: Light find my hand. Light find my path. Let the Sword of Light answer, and let it fade when the shadows loosen. Never say it twice in the same dark.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I have both. I won't waste them.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Use the first when you feel yourself slipping. Use the second only when the pale hands reach you — not before.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: Thank you, Hanash.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Don't thank me. Just survive, so this was not wasted breath.

transcript.speaker: Salim
transcript.text: I will remember what you told me.

transcript.speaker: Hanash
transcript.text: Remember only what keeps you standing. Now go. Don't look back at the fountain.
